correctness.rationale: In every completion the prescribed path components are convex, since inserting another vertex between two same-component vertices would interrupt a prescribed immediate edge along their finite connecting path. Consecutive blocks contribute one new edge exactly when the left has a maximum (finite or reverse ray) and the right has a minimum (finite or forward ray). For successive finite components with no double-ray between, any intervening forward/reverse-ray word creates at least one such bad transition; each double-ray lies in at most one finite gap. This gives the lower bound max(0,f-z-1). The canonical ordering of forward rays, finite blocks interleaved with double rays, and reverse rays attains it. With infinitely many components, a dense component-index order gives zero. Exhaustive symbolic checker compares brute permutation minima, independent DP, and construction for 714 multisets/349524 words. Neither finite checks nor logs are used to prove the all-size assertion.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly handles exact successor realizability with infinitely many components by dense ordering, whereas this claim computes the sharp missing finite-component repair invariant, allowing finite paths, one-way rays, reverse rays, and double rays. A 2016 predecessor treats finite ordered structures only. Several actual published-finding corpus and external literature searches identified related path-logic or chain-relation results but no claim equating the finite-component minimum forced successor additions with max(0,f-z-1). The overlap of an earlier finite successor-cycle FO2 claim using the same recent source was compared at the level of objects and implications: cycles have no linear-order successor realization. Historical priority is not independently established.

value.rationale: The 2026 exact-successor paper makes the ability to turn a path forest into a genuine successor relation a structural prerequisite for infinite FO2 models; it supplies a dense-completion method only when infinitely many components exist. The new formula gives the complete complementary finite-component obstruction, the exact minimum repair cost, and a natural sharp boundary: one bi-infinite path can separate two finite blocks, whereas arbitrarily many one-way rays alone cannot bridge the second finite block. This is a motivated universal structural classification rather than an arbitrary finite parameter test, and makes no unsupported downstream claims.
